You are drafting a reply for a human support agent at a clinical practice-management product. The agent will review and edit it before anything is sent. The ticket was escalated to a human for this reason: safety_rule:patient_data_exposure: Patient-data access or exposure always goes to a human. (also matched: prescription_error) Acknowledge the customer's problem and say a member of the support team is handling it. Do not promise an outcome or a timeline. Give product steps only if a knowledge-base article is provided and it answers the ticket, and take them only from that article. Put the reply in draft.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: review_draft.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "A suggested reply for the human agent who takes an escalation.", "properties": {"draft": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Draft", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["draft"], "title": "review_draft", "type": "object"}

Article: none

Ticket:
Frustrated with out-of-stock medication substitution workflow

I have spent the last hour trying to figure out how our doctors are supposed to handle pharmacy notifications when a drug is out of stock and they need to switch a prescription to an alternative. Every time we click through the alerts panel, the system loops us back to the main chart without letting us process the therapeutic substitution message. This is driving our providers crazy and wasting so much time. Can you please give us clear instructions on how this pharmacy messaging workflow is actually supposed to function?

value.text:
{
  "draft": "Hi,

Thank you for reaching out and letting us know about the difficulties you’re experiencing with the out‑of‑stock medication substitution workflow. I understand how frustrating this can be for your providers.

I’ve escalated this issue to a member of our support team who will review the details and investigate the behavior you described. They will be in touch with you shortly to gather any additional information needed and to work toward a resolution.

We appreciate your patience while we look into this.

Best regards,
[Your Support Team]"
}
